raw_segments.text: Katarina Ivanovna's body was still lying in the coffin.
S. Vidrigaev was busy making arrangements for the funeral.
At their last meeting, S. Vidrigaev informed Raskolnikov that he had made an arrangement,
and a very satisfactory one, for Katarina Ivanovna's children.
That he had, through certain connections, succeeded in getting hold of certain personages
by whose help the three orphans could be at once placed in very suitable institutions.
That the money he had settled on them had been of great assistance,
as it is much easier to place orphans with some property than destitute ones.
He said something, too, about Sanya, and promised to come himself in a day or two
to see Raskolnikov, mentioning that he would like to consult with him
that there were things they must talk over.
